regressions.issue: The encoder's length now keeps '_4 - mem[64]', which is 0: _4 was read from mem[64] just before, and the encoding loop writes only at mem[64] + 64 + 96*i. The loop bound reads the memory copy's length mem[128] instead of stor72.length, which was just stored there.
regressions.rule: Writes at mem[64] + k with k >= 32 (or at any address above the free-pointer floor) never alias mem[64], so a held read b = mem[64] stays equal to mem[64] and 'b - mem[64]' folds to 0. A read of a word just stored with a known value prints as that value.
regressions.verified: reading only (mem[128] = stor72.length at 401; no store to 64 between 426 and 436)
